summary: Don A. Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, and was appointed Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem circa 1972.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Richmond College, Galle, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, under George Uglow Pope and Wilhelm Geiger, and held posts with the Ceylon government and the University of London.

Donald A. Ringe specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Kentucky, University of Oxford, and Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill, and taught at Bard College (1983–1985) before becoming Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Ching-yu Wang, also studying under Akira Takeda, and took up a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst circa 1976.

Donald Eric Capps was a religious studies scholar who studied at Lewis & Clark College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, Phillips University, and Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).
Donald Ferguson was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Denmark Hill Grammar School, Regent's Park College, and University College London.
Donald Harper is a sinologist. He held positions at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and the University of Chicago, where he was Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer works in Buddhist and religious studies. Mentored by Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai, he held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004), Chiang Mai University, and Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University and Harvard University, learning under Wm. Theodore de Bary. He held academic posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (from 1955).

Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who earned degrees at Knox College and Washington University in St. Louis. He served as department chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College, Oxford (1988) and Sapienza University of Rome (1996).

Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere. He has held academic posts at Bucknell, Michigan, Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006–2012), and the University of Texas at Austin.

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held a post at Middlebury College (1986), and joined the University of Michigan faculty in 1990 as a distinguished professor.

Donald Wiebe is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He has held a post at Trinity College, Toronto (circa 1980) and served as General Editor for Toronto Studies in Religion (attested 1996).
Dondub Buddhayin was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who served as Abbot of Chilttai Monastery and Ganden Dargye Ling (attested 1933). He also taught Eugène Obermiller.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Dongak Tendzin was a scholar who studied under and taught both Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye. He also studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and taught Shechen Gyaltsab.

Dongchu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1934–1945) and abbot of Dinghui Monastery (~1945–1949).

Donna C. Kurtz is an archaeologist and historian. She studied at the University of Cincinnati, Yale University, and the University of Oxford, where she later worked (~1970–2011), holding posts at the Beazley Archive and the Classical Art Research Centre.
